pairs.evidence: app/(studio)/ledger/_ledger/read.ts:224 The ledger is hash-chained (kernel events.ts), but the screen serves every event without recomputing the chain or showing any integrity verdict, and nothing in app/, lib/, pipeline/ or workers/ calls the kernel's verify, so tamper evidence is only checked by tests and a manual Python CLI.

techniques.evidence: app/(studio)/ledger/_ledger/read.ts:224 Rung 3 is built on the write side, but no verify on read: no verified/tampered verdict on the interactive surface.

app/(studio)/ledger/_ledger/read.ts:15 Keyset pages, facet counts over the whole filter, capped/scanned/exhausted shown on the surface (List.tsx:123, Toolbar.tsx:122). Gap: reads of the trail are not themselves recorded.

app/(studio)/ledger/_ledger/vocab.ts:95 The detail shows the effective time plus a derived/recorded chip and the recorded `at`. Gap: the from/to window ranges over coalesce(occurredAt, at) without naming that clock in the interface.
app/(studio)/ledger/_ledger/actions.ts:3 The screen's server actions are reads only; no mutation surface is exposed.
app/(studio)/ledger/page.tsx:1 Rows are never invalidated, so there is no record interval to rewind.

pairs.subject: audit-logging
pairs.evidence: packages/kernel/py/verify_events.py:173 The verifier keeps only the optional columns it knows and silently ignores any other, so a newer events schema adding a covered column would make this reader recompute without it and report 'hash mismatch: the row's content changed after it was written' (tampered) instead of 'written by a newer version'.

techniques.evidence: packages/kernel/py/verify_events.py:173 Absent-not-null holds (line 129 drops NULL columns), but an unknown covered column is not refused as a version verdict; the verdict set is intact/tampered only.

packages/kernel/py/verify_events.py:152 A chain with serialized writers (BEGIN IMMEDIATE) and an external anchor for a cut tail; the digest is unkeyed sha256, which events.ts says plainly ('tamper-evident, not tamper-proof').
packages/kernel/py/kernel_ledger.py:35 The Python ledger module exports append and nothing that mutates.
packages/kernel/py/kernel_ledger.py:12 One Python append shared by lease and job writers.
packages/kernel/py/kernel_ledger.py:37 A control-record inversion: the event commits with the state or the act fails, as documented.
packages/kernel/py/kernel_ledger.py:18 The ledger is the origin of the fact here, so one clock is correct and occurredAt is never written.
packages/kernel/py/job.py:356 str(exception) from any worker drive goes into hashed, permanent ledger data with no size cap or scrub.

pairs.registryProposal: absent-not-null-in-hashed-records speaks of record keys; on a relational store the unknown 'key' is an unknown column, and a verifier that selects columns by a hard-coded list (PRAGMA table_info filtered against it) is the column-shaped form of the same failure. Naming it would help.
